verdict.line: You lose if you let him fight you at full HP or get caught with E on cooldown; you win by poking his regen down and kiting him into a slow death.

brief.thesis: Dr. Mundo's passive (Adrenaline Rush) heals a percentage of his max HP every second, so flat trades only feed him sustain he regenerates back within seconds. Gnar's entire job is ranged poke with Q (Boomerang Throw) and kiting with E (Hop) to outpace his regen rather than out-damage it in a single trade, which lines up with the near-even 48.9% head-to-head over 141 games despite Gnar holding the lane and solo-kill edge.

theirWindow.when: your E on cooldown, he's in range
theirWindow.what: He has no gap-closer of his own but once he's stuck to you in melee range with W (Burning Agony) ticking, you can't disengage — this is when he kills you. Never let your E be down while he's within his 325-range W radius.

yourWindow.when: his W (Burning Agony) draining, low HP
yourWindow.what: W burns his own health to deal continual damage and shorten disables, so every second he holds it on, his Adrenaline Rush is fighting its own ability. Poke with Q (Boomerang Throw, 1100 range) while he's low and before he can use R (Sadism) to reset the fight — R only gives movement speed and HP regen, no damage, so out-trading him before level 6 ult access is free value.

start.why: 49.6% win rate over 119 games and the dominant pick (66.9%); the lifesteal and AD help you contest trades against his self-healing instead of getting outlasted.

boots.why: 45.6% win rate over 79 games and the top pick (45.1%); his Q (Infected Cleaver) and autos are physical-heavy, and the attack speed shred on his sustained poke outweighs taking Mercury's Treads here.

core.why: Core first item on 50% of winning builds; the stats spike powers your Hyper (W) bonus damage and gives the movement speed to kite him when your E is down.
Second item in every major build path; the armor shred and sustained damage matter against a target that regenerates HP every second.
Most common third item (22% of games); the HP and damage reduction buffer protect you if he catches you with his W draining on top of you.

situational.when: he builds tanky and your autos need more sustained magic damage to break his regen
he's rushing lifesteal or healing items and you need the grievous wounds to cut his sustain
his Adrenaline Rush healing is outpacing your poke damage
you're ahead and want to snowball true damage on-hit through his HP pool

runes.keystoneWhy: Run on the top page (50% win rate, 23.9% pick); the scaling attack speed rewards extended poke exchanges rather than one burst window, which fits fighting his regen down over time instead of all-in.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport is run in 74.9% of games at 50.7% win rate; Teleport lets you reset and return to lane after poking him down rather than committing to an all-in he can heal back from.

playing.title: Poke, don't commit
playing.detail: Throw Q (Boomerang Throw) at max range whenever it's up — the slow on hit and catch-reduced cooldown reward you for landing it without entering his W (Burning Agony) radius.

playing.title: Track his E (Masochism) window
playing.detail: His AD spikes based on missing HP for a few seconds after he casts it; back off auto-trades the moment you see this buff proc rather than standing in it.

playing.title: Hold E for disengage, not engage
playing.detail: Hop's bounce off his head is tempting as an all-in tool, but save it to create distance after poking — his passive heal punishes you for staying in extended melee range.

playing.title: Punish before level 6
playing.detail: He has no hard engage and R (Sadism) only grants movement speed and regen, not damage, so your Q poke advantage is largest before he hits 6 and can sustain through longer fights.

playing.title: Reset on Teleport, don't force all-ins
playing.detail: Since trades rarely one-shot through Adrenaline Rush, use Teleport to return after recalling rather than trying to end lane with a single fight.

playing.title: Respect the W drain in melee
playing.detail: The moment he's within 325 range and W is ticking, his damage and disable-reduction both increase — this is his only real power spike in a direct fight, so don't contest it stationary.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and win-rate figures are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.20.1); the mechanical reasoning and trade timing are my own tactical read, not sourced from the data.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid being chased when [E] is on cooldown as he will kill you. Focus on managing your distance while kiting him constantly.
